question.text: Does TDP-43 type confer a distinct pattern of atrophy in frontotemporal lobar degeneration?

medgemma_4b.clinical_reasoning: TDP-43 proteinopathy is a hallmark of frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD). The characteristic pattern of atrophy in FTLD, particularly TDP-43 type, involves prominent atrophy of the frontal and temporal lobes, which is consistent with the name of the disease. Therefore, TDP-43 type FTLD is associated with a distinct pattern of atrophy.
medgemma_4b.critical_evidence: TDP-43 proteinopathy is a hallmark of frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD).
medgemma_4b.differential_considered: Other forms of FTLD exist (e.g., FTLD-Tau, FTLD-C9orf72), and these may have different patterns of atrophy. However, TDP-43 type FTLD is the most common and has a characteristic pattern of frontal and temporal lobe atrophy.

rnj1_8b.clinical_reasoning: TDP-43 mutations are associated with a more anteriorly focused atrophy pattern in frontotemporal lobar degeneration, particularly involving the frontal and anterior temporal lobes, compared to other FTLD subtypes. This distinct pattern is supported by neuropathological findings and imaging studies showing greater involvement of the anterior frontal and temporal regions in TDP-43-positive cases.
rnj1_8b.critical_evidence: Neuropathological studies consistently demonstrate a more anterior atrophy pattern in TDP-43-positive FTLD compared to other FTLD subtypes
rnj1_8b.differential_considered: Considered MAPT mutations (tauopathy) which show more posterior involvement, and C9orf72 which has variable patterns, but TDP-43 shows the most distinct anterior pattern

qwen3_vl_8b.clinical_reasoning: TDP-43 proteinopathy is a hallmark of a subset of frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD), and it is associated with distinct atrophy patterns, particularly involving the frontal and anterior temporal lobes, often with relative sparing of the posterior temporal lobes compared to other FTLD subtypes. This pattern is more consistent with behavioral variant FTD and non-fluent aphasia variants.
qwen3_vl_8b.critical_evidence: TDP-43-positive FTLD shows preferential atrophy in frontal and anterior temporal regions, differentiating it from tau-positive FTLD (e.g., Pick’s disease) which often shows more posterior temporal involvement.
qwen3_vl_8b.differential_considered: Tau-positive FTLD (Pick’s disease) was considered but ruled out due to its different atrophy pattern (posterior temporal predominance), and Alzheimer’s disease was excluded due to lack of hippocampal atrophy and amyloid pathology.
